claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have a son, Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with you at home.

Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to ask:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care? For example, do you provide for his day-to-day needs like food, clothes, and accommodation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I look after him every day - I provide all his food, clothes, and everything else he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. A few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation provided by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, yes - Alex has been in hospital for a while now. He's been there for a few months.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see, thank you for letting me know. This is an important detail as it can affect Child Benefit eligibility.

**Can you tell me more specifically how long Alex has been in hospital? And during this time, have you been regularly spending money on him (for example, on clothes, toys, books, or other items for him)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in hospital for 12 weeks now. And yes, I've been spending money on him - I buy him clothes, books, toys, things like that to keep him comfortable while he's there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Just to clarify:

**Has Alex been in hospital continuously for exactly 12 weeks, or has it been more than 12 weeks? And is he in a hospital here in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been exactly 12 weeks, and yes, he's in a hospital here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I need to ask one more important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, such as another parent or family member?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✓ Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
✓ He normally lives with you in the UK
✓ You're responsible for his care and provide for his needs
✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

Although Alex has been in hospital for 12 weeks (which is normally the threshold where Child Benefit might be affected), you qualify for an important exception: because you're regularly spending money on Alex during his hospital stay - buying him clothes, books, toys, and other items - you can continue to receive Child Benefit.

This exception applies specifically to children in UK hospitals when the parent regularly spends money on them during their stay.

If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit, you can apply for it. If you're already receiving it and were concerned about Alex's hospital stay, you can continue to claim as long as you keep regularly spending money on him.

According to the rules, there is an exception to the 12-week hospital rule for children in UK hospitals if the parent regularly spends money on them. Since the claimant meets this exception and no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, the claimant is eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
